Plan_Intro
data.value: What your organization may use, and how much it uses now. Ask the platform owner to change a plan.

data.name: Plan_EditorIntro
data.value: Choose the plan, and override single limits for this tenant. Use the Custom plan for agreements made per customer.

data.name: Plan_OverrideHelp
data.value: Override: leave blank to follow the plan, type a number to set a limit, or type unlimited to lift it. For history, unlimited keeps everything.

data.name: Limits_Intro
data.value: The limits of each plan. They apply to every tenant on that plan unless the tenant has its own override. Changes take effect at once; history is trimmed to the new period within hours.

data.name: Limits_CustomHelp
data.value: For agreements per customer; set the values per tenant.

data.name: Limits_Blank
data.value: Leave a number blank for unlimited. History blank keeps everything. Domains count assets of type domain, endpoints count hosts with a port or found in certificate logs.

data.name: Limit_Domains

data.value: Enter a public domain name to see its TLS certificate and its DNS email and security records. Nothing is stored.

data.name: Scan_Err_invalid
data.value: Enter a public domain name such as example.com, without a port or path. Addresses and local names are not checked.

data.name: Scan_Err_rate_limited
data.value: You checked a lot of domains recently. Try again later.

data.name: Scan_Err_busy
data.value: The checker is busy. Try again in a minute.

data.name: Scan_Err_disabled
data.value: The public checker is not available.

data.value: Nothing about this check is stored. Only the certificate on port 443 and public DNS records are looked at.

data.name: Scan_NextText
data.value: This is a single look. FullyQualified checks every domain on a schedule, tells you when a certificate is about to expire or a record changes, and turns it into a NIS2 report.

data.name: Limits_IntervalHelp
data.value: The interval is how long a result stays fresh before an asset is checked again; checks run on a one-minute rhythm, so the shortest is one minute. Blank uses the server default (Scanning:IntervalHours). A failed check is always retried after 15 minutes.

data.name: CheckAll_Text
data.value: Queue every check of every asset right away instead of waiting for the next round. You can do this once every {0} minutes.

data.name: CheckAll_Queued
data.value: {0} checks queued. The results appear within a minute; follow them on the Log page.

data.name: CheckAll_Cooldown
data.value: You just did this. Try again in {0} minute(s).

data.name: CheckAll_AlreadyQueued
data.value: Everything is already waiting to be checked.

data.name: Diag_Intro
data.value: Checks that FullyQualified is set up to do its job for your organization: your plan, whether checks are running, whether alarms reach you and whether you can recover from a lost passkey. Nothing is changed.

data.name: Diag_SendAlarm
data.value: Also send a test alarm through every channel

data.name: Diag_RoomLeft
data.value: There is room left for everything.

data.name: Diag_AtLimit
data.value: Limit reached for: {0}. Adding more is refused until you remove something or the plan is raised.

data.name: Diag_NoAssets

data.name: Diag_Stale

data.name: Diag_AlarmsOff

data.name: Diag_AlarmsOn

data.name: Diag_NotDelivered

data.name: Diag_NotSent
data.value: No test alarm was sent because alarms are switched off.

data.name: Diag_RecentFailed
data.value: {0} of {1} alarms in the last 7 days failed to deliver. See the Log page.

data.name: Diag_AdminsOk
data.value: There are {0} administrators, so one can help the other.

data.name: Diag_OneAdmin
data.value: There is only one administrator. If that person loses their passkey, only the platform owner or the server operator can help. Invite a second administrator.

data.name: Diag_PasskeysOk
data.value: Every administrator has more than one way to sign in.

data.name: Diag_PasskeysFew
data.value: {0} administrator(s) have a single passkey and no single sign-on. Ask them to add a second device on the Account page.

data.name: Diag_HttpsOk
data.value: You are using {0}, which passkeys accept.

data.name: Diag_NotHttps
data.value: This page is served over plain http at {0}. Passkeys only work over HTTPS (or on localhost), so other people cannot sign in.

data.name: Diag_OriginDiffers
data.value: Auth:Origin is {0} but you are using {1}. Passkeys are tied to the configured address, so sign-in will fail.

data.name: Diag_ProxyHeaders
data.value: Requests arrive through a proxy, but forwarded headers are not switched on (ASPNETCORE_FORWARDEDHEADERS_ENABLED). Visitors will share one address, which breaks per-address limits.

data.name: Diag_MigrationsOk
data.value: The database is up to date.

data.name: Diag_MigrationsPending
data.value: {0} database migrations are not applied. Restart the app with Database:AutoMigrate on, or apply them by hand.

data.name: Diag_KeysOk
data.value: Sign-in keys are stored in the database, so sessions survive a restart.

data.name: Diag_KeysNone
data.value: No sign-in keys are stored yet; people are signed out when the app restarts until one is created.

data.name: Diag_NoSmtpHost

data.name: Diag_SsoDown

data.name: Diag_NoSso
data.value: Single sign-on is not configured; people sign in with passkeys.

data.name: Diag_SsoOpenText
data.value: Sso:AutoProvision is on without Sso:AllowedDomains, so anyone whose email the provider has verified can create an account.
